item.title: Lautoka residents raise alarm over public drinking and grab-and-runs
item.description: Residents and taxi drivers in Lautoka are calling for increased police patrols as concerns grow over public drinking, nuisance behaviour and grab-and-run incidents in the city. Taxi driver Navneet Ram told fijivillage News that groups of people are frequently seen drinking alcohol in public areas, particularly during weekends, raising concerns for the safety of families and other members of the pu
item.content:encoded:
Residents and taxi drivers in Lautoka are calling for increased police patrols as concerns grow over public drinking, nuisance behaviour and grab-and-run incidents in the city.

Taxi driver Navneet Ram told fijivillage News that groups of people are frequently seen drinking alcohol in public areas, particularly during weekends, raising concerns for the safety of families and other members of the public.

Ram says some of the common areas where people gather to drink include the Tukani car park towards the seaside, Syria Line behind Ramesh Investment, Tukani Street in front of Kiran Palace, Marine Drive, and areas along Yasawa Street near City Mall.

He says public drinking is also common near a corner shop located about 200 metres from the police station, particularly from Thursdays to Saturdays.

Ram adds that taxi drivers have often tried to address the behaviour but are ignored.

He says it is concerning that people are drinking in public spaces where families and children spend time.

Ram says while the Lautoka City Council has made improvements to parks and other public areas following numerous requests, it is disappointing to see some people misusing these spaces by drinking alcohol and urinating there.

Meanwhile, Ram has also raised concerns about youths allegedly being involved in grab-and-run incidents, adding he recently witnessed two robberies however, no report was lodged with Police.

Ram says, as a taxi driver, he is concerned not only for his own safety but also for the safety of people particularly kids.

He is calling on Police to increase patrols in known trouble spots to help address public drinking, nuisance behaviour and grab-and-run incidents.

Ram is also calling for stricter laws, with people caught drinking in public and creating nuisances facing hefty fines or imprisonment.

item.title: Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist Dr Nanise Sikiti to share her story on fijivillage Her-Story
item.description: From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination. Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono tonight at 7pm.
item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono tonight at 7pm.

Dr Sikiti will share the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She will also speak about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

You can watch fijivillage Her-Story on our facebook page, YouTube channel, and TikTok and X account, fijivillage at 7pm tonight.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Her-Story on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: Uciwai residents reject temporary fixes as FRA looks into road concerns
item.description: Residents of Uciwai, Nadi, say they are still waiting for a lasting solution to their deteriorating road, with the Fiji Roads Authority saying it is looking into the concerns raised. Uciwai resident Seleima Wati Evans says the community has been raising concerns about potholes, dust and the condition of the road for several years.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Uciwai, Nadi, say they are still waiting for a lasting solution to their deteriorating road, with the Fiji Roads Authority saying it is looking into the concerns raised.

Uciwai resident Seleima Wati Evans says the community has been raising concerns about potholes, dust and the condition of the road for several years.

Evans says the situation is particularly concerning for people living close to the roadside, especially school students who are exposed to dust generated by passing vehicles.

She says she recently lodged another complaint with the Fiji Roads Authority and followed the required process by collecting signatures from residents through a petition.

She says letters of support have also been received from community representatives and businesses in the area, highlighting the impact the road condition is having on the community.

Evans says Uciwai advisory councillor Mahendra Reddy has also raised concerns about the condition of the road and its impact on residents and businesses.

She says previous repair work has failed to provide a lasting solution, with potholes patched and sections of the road repaired only for the problems to return.

Evans says residents want the road to be properly repaired rather than relying on temporary fixes.

She says the deteriorating road continues to affect residents and businesses, while the dust remains a concern for families living along the roadside.

Evans says residents should not have to continue living with the same road conditions after years of raising their concerns.

The Fiji Roads Authority says it is looking into the matter.

item.title: No objections raised against proposed new AOG Fiji headquarters
item.description: People living in and around Anand Street were given an opportunity to raise questions or concerns about the proposed development as part of the EIA process. Representatives from the Department of Environment, engineers, architects, construction representatives, relevant authorities and members of the public attended the consultation.
item.content:encoded:
People living in and around Anand Street were given an opportunity to raise questions or concerns about the proposed development as part of the EIA process.

Representatives from the Department of Environment, engineers, architects, construction representatives, relevant authorities and members of the public attended the consultation.

WesEng Consulting PTE Limited Principal EIA Consultant and Civil Engineer Andrew Singh says the consultation provided an opportunity to hear the views of people who could be affected by the development.

Singh says the EIA report is expected to be submitted to the Department of Environment within the next three to four weeks.

He says construction of the proposed development is expected to take about 15 months.

The proposed seven-level building will include car parking, office spaces, meeting facilities, a deck and lobby.

The development will also include new water and sewerage systems, stormwater drainage, driveways, fire hydrants and a new access road.

item.title: Waqanika’s defence to call up to 5 witnesses in FICAC trial
item.description: The counsel for Tanya Waqanika, Barbara Malimali, has revealed in the Suva Magistrates Court today that they will call four to five witnesses in Waqanika’s FICAC trial. Waqanika appeared before Magistrate Yogesh Prasad this morning.
item.content:encoded:
The counsel for Tanya Waqanika, Barbara Malimali, has revealed in the Suva Magistrates Court today that they will call four to five witnesses in Waqanika’s FICAC trial.

Waqanika appeared before Magistrate Yogesh Prasad this morning.

FICAC counsel Joseph Work says the prosecution will also call four to five witnesses.

Magistrate Yogesh Prasad says former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad’s FICAC trial may continue for another two to three weeks and could spill over into the dates currently set for Waqanika’s trial.

He says the trial dates may therefore need to be shifted.

Malimali says the defence is also keeping an eye on Professor Prasad’s case.

Waqanika’s trial is currently scheduled from September 28th to October 2nd.

She is charged with one count of publicly indicating opposition to a political party.

It is alleged that on or about April 19th, 2024, while serving as a public officer, namely as a board member of Investment Fiji and Telecom Fiji Limited, Waqanika publicly indicated opposition to SODELPA.
